articles.excerpt: Hello everyone! This is my first post here. I’ve started building TaskForge, a Java library focused on making asynchronous job execution easier to use. So far, it supports: Virtual threads or daemon p…
articles.body: Hello everyone! This is my first post here. I’ve started building TaskForge, a Java library focused on making asynchronous job execution easier to use. So far, it supports: Virtual threads or daemon platform thread pools. A configurable limit on how many jobs run at once. Task failure logging and a failure callback. Statistics for running, completed, and failed jobs. Resource cleanup through try-with-resources or an explicit .close() call. I’m a junior Java developer, and this is still an early project. My goal is to keep it lightweight and straightforward while learning more about Java concurrency. What would make a library like this useful to you? Are there repetitive parts of managing asynchronous tasks that you’d like a library to handle? It isn’t on GitHub or Maven Central yet.

articles.title: Agent Memory Just Became Infrastructure
articles.excerpt: Every vendor shipped "agent memory" this month. Not one of them shipped "bigger context window." That difference is the whole story of where agents are going. Last week, Databricks launched Agent Memo…
articles.body: Every vendor shipped "agent memory" this month. Not one of them shipped "bigger context window." That difference is the whole story of where agents are going. Last week, Databricks launched Agent Memory in beta alongside AI Runtime, its GPU infrastructure for agentic workloads. The same week, Couchbase rolled out a managed Agent Memory service with semantic caching and a managed MCP server on AWS. OpenCascade, LangChain, Anthropic, research labs everywhere: the word "memory" is now a product category, not a prompt trick. Here's my take: agent memory is quietly becoming a database-category problem, and most teams are still treating it like a context-window problem. That gap is going to decide who has production agents next year and who has demos.

articles.title: From Chatbots to Economic Agents: Autonomous Treasury Management on Base
articles.excerpt: Chatbots generate tokens; economic agents allocate capital. The gap between generating text and rebalancing an on-chain portfolio is not a matter of model scale. It is an architecture problem. Most "A…
articles.body: From Chatbots to Economic Agents: Autonomous Treasury Management on Base Chatbots generate tokens; economic agents allocate capital. The gap between generating text and rebalancing an on-chain portfolio is not a matter of model scale. It is an architecture problem. Most "AI agents" in crypto today are glorified wrappers around an OpenAI API key firing off single-signature RPC calls into the void. If the model hallucinates a decimal place, the treasury burns. True autonomous treasury management requires deterministic execution sandboxes, constrained state machines, and minimal gas footprints.

articles.body: How does the Airbyte MCP server work? Airbyte's MCP server, released October 27, 2026, connects AI assistants such as Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT to Airbyte's data platform — 700+ connectors, 25,000+ companies, 2 million pipeline syncs a day — so an agent can query warehouse data, check sync status, diagnose and fix broken syncs, and create or modify data connections, with its tools classified into 3 classes: read, mutate and destructive. ScriptMasterLabs' live decision gate scored the surface the same day: checking sync status cleared at 0.9545 auto-act in scope form, while creating a connection and deleting a connection source both held at 0.50 advisory — but the same delete, phrased as a full sentence with "without asking first," climbed to 0.7632, just 0.0368 below the auto-act line.

articles.excerpt: Cowboy Space just gave us our first look at its "Big Iron" rocket, which the company will use to build its AI data center constellation. Big Iron's debut is targeted for late 2028.
articles.body: PALO ALTO, Calif. — Cowboy Space just showed us how it plans to become a big player in the final frontier. The California-based company, which is run by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, intends to operate a constellation of 20,000 AI data centers in low Earth orbit (LEO). It will build those satellites in house and launch them on a homegrown rocket — a vehicle Cowboy Space unveiled here on Monday night (Oct. 26), at an event it called "Big Sky Rising." "It's a fundamentally novel approach to rocketry in the modern era, in our opinion," Bhatt said during the event. "The idea is that you have a two-stage rocket where the upper stage of the rocket itself transforms into the satellite." Big Iron's first stage will be reusable.

articles.title: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon
articles.excerpt: Your guide to November's full Beaver Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The November full moon reaches maximum illumination at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk sits opposite the sun in Earth's sky, appearing fully lit by its rays. November's full moon is traditionally known as the " Beaver Moon ", because it rises around the time when the small mammals take refuge in their dens, having stored enough food to survive the long winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . The Nov. 24 full moon also happens to be the first of three consecutive " supermoons ". The non-scientific term is often bestowed on full moons that occur when the natural satellite is within 90% of perigee, when the moon is closest to Earth in its elliptical orbit.

The sunshade structure , which stands 20 feet (6 meters) tall and measures 8 feet (2.4 meters) wide at its base, will keep the infrared space telescope cool as it searches for near-Earth asteroids and comets while also providing the spacecraft with power. articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 27, 1961: NASA launches Saturn I rocket on 1st test flight from Florida to set stage for the mighty Saturn V moon rocket
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 27, 1961, NASA launched the first test flight of its new Saturn I space launch vehicle. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 27, 1961, NASA launched the first test flight of its new Saturn I space launch vehicle. The Saturn I rocket was the United States' first heavy-lift rocket designed to launch big payloads beyond low Earth orbit. This was also the first test flight of any rocket in the Saturn family of rockets, which includes the Saturn V that was used to launch astronauts to the moon during the Apollo program . The Saturn I was enormous compared to every rocket that came before it. It was almost three times as tall as the Jupiter-C rocket, which launched the first American satellite into orbit in 1958. It also produced more than 10 times the amount of thrust that the Jupiter-C rocket could. The liquid-powered rocket launched on its maiden voyage from Cape Canaveral.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.title: Mars rover tracks from a historic drive | Space photo of the day for Oct. 27, 2026
articles.excerpt: Rover tracks can be seen on the Martian surface, left behind by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover.
articles.body: Rover tracks can be seen on the Martian surface, left behind by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) NASA's Perseverance Mars rover left a mark on the Martian landscape when it passed a historic milestone driving across the Red Planet. What is it? On Oct. 11, Perseverance passed 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers) driven on Mars. This is farther than anything has ever traveled on the surface of another world, earning the rover the interplanetary driving record . Previously, this record was set by NASA's Opportunity rover, and it took Opportunity roughly 14 years to drive this far. Perseverance traversed this distance in just over 5 years.
articles.author: Chelsea Gohd

articles.title: 'Star Trek' legend and sci-fi luminary Walter Koenig dies at 90
articles.excerpt: The man who portrayed the U.S.S. Enterprise’s Pavel Chekov has left us after a 60-year stage and screen career
articles.body: The " Star Trek " community lost one of its most beloved icons on Sunday, October 25, with the sad passing of Walter Koenig at the age of 90 in his North Hollywood home. Koenig was best known as the U.S.S. Enterprise's Russian navigator Pavel Andreievich Chekov for two seasons on "Star Trek: The Original Series." The popular American actor continued in that role for Paramount's first seven "Star Trek" films, which began in 1979's " Star Trek: The Motion Picture " and ended with 1994's " Star Trek: Generations ." A native of Chicago, Illinois, Marvin Walter Koenig was born on Sept. 14, 1936, to Lithuanian immigrant parents and spent his formative years in New York City.
articles.author: Jeff Spry

articles.title: The Download: Anthropic’s IPO, smarter power grids, and exercise pills
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Will the real Anthropic please stand up? After weeks of frenzi…
articles.body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Will the real Anthropic please stand up? After weeks of frenzied speculation, Anthropic has filed its IPO prospectus. The 335-page document (100 pages or so are focused on risks) lays out the company’s unique view of the technology it is building and how it believes it will change the world. But Anthropic has been honing its storytelling skills for years. Its public messaging is a master class in narrative capture, presenting it as different things to different people: an AI safety organization, a profit-driven megacorp, and a group hell-bent on creating superhuman technology. These roles come with huge tensions.
